# `set_plan`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Create or update legacy autosave plans from an array of plan objects.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xd1e10, ParsePlans @0x311710, SetPlan @0x30e350 (64-bit build) |

Parses an array of legacy plan objects, merges each into the plan with the same id (copying the existing plan first, so omitted members keep their prior values; new plans take documented defaults), commits them to the global plan map, updates the capture settings and persists the result. While the device is exposing, an enabled plan is only updated through its special options. Before applying, the first enabled parsed plan is size-checked against free disk space (estimate plus a 150 MB reserve); the check is bypassed when no parsed plan is enabled or when the estimate is lower than that of the existing enabled plan. Malformed roots and non-string sequence type/suffix values have no reliable error contract.

Side effects: Replaces entries of the global legacy plan map, updates the enabled-plan and capture settings and writes them to storage (the save result is ignored). The precheck can refresh cached estimates, camera information and log output even when it then rejects. No exposure is started by the call.

| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_plan"`. [READ] |
| `params` | array<object> | no | - | Array of plan objects. The root type is not checked: an object whose member values are plan objects is also walked (member names ignored), a bare plan object is not equivalent to a one-plan array, an empty array is accepted, and omitted or null params have no reliable behaviour (the parser dereferences the missing value). Clients MUST send an array. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | A plan, target or sequence id is missing, not an integer or INT_MIN | `invalid id` |
| 108 | A recognized target_coord member is malformed | `expected float param` |
| 224 | Restricted fields of an exposed enabled plan are edited while on the exposing page | `cannot edit sequence unless reset the progress` |
| 208 | Free space does not cover the estimate of the first enabled plan plus a 150 MB reserve (see description for the bypass) | `disk is full` |
| 268 | The plan loader thread is running | `operation is in progress` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, minimal - One plan, id only (shape READ, values invented):

```json
{"id":31,"method":"set_plan","params":[{"id":1}]}
```

Request, with-target - A plan with one target and one sequence (values invented):

```json
{"id":32,"method":"set_plan","params":[{"id":1,"plan_name":"Example plan","enable":true,"start_time":{"type":"date","hour":21},"end_time":{"type":"dawn"},"targets":[{"id":1,"target_name":"Example target","target_coord":[12,30],"seqs":[{"id":1,"type":"light","exp":10,"gain":80,"bin":1,"repeat":30}]}]}]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_plan","result":0,"code":0,"id":31}
```

Reply, missing-id:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_plan","error":"invalid id","code":200,"id":33}
```
